name: Read the Room: Know the World

ios.desc:
A question is chosen by the public and highlighted as the Question of the Day. It drops at a random time, and everyone answers it live. Interactive maps and visualizations are produced to explore the responses. 

You can also:
- Compare how different cities and countries think
- Compare how your network thinks vs the rest of the world

Why Read the Room is different:
- Privacy-first by design. No logins or signups to identify you. No ads and no algorithm designed to keep you scrolling. Just honest answers captured in a fun environment showing interesting patterns. 

We're free and open-source, and designed to facilitate authentic interactions between humans pseudonymously.

Whether you're settling a debate with friends, testing a hypothesis, or wondering how your city thinks compared to others, Read the Room is the place to ask!

android.desc:
A question chosen by the public to be highlighted once a day. The world answers anonymously. See how your city and and your extended friend network compares to the world via interactive maps and charts.

No likes. No followers. No algorithm.

🗺️ LIVE COMPARISON MAPS
Compare how opinions distribute across cities, and across your social graph. Find out if you're typical for your area or if you're the black sheep in your friend group.

📱 HOME SCREEN WIDGETS
Question of the Day on your home screen. Check the pulse of the planet without notifications or noise.

🔒 PRIVACY-FIRST ARCHITECTURE
Most data stays on your device. Only aggregate patterns go public. No tracking and data selling.

💡 THE IDEA
We're building a human bioindicator and social barometer. A way to sense how our communities think and feel in real time without an algorithm deciding what matters. 

Anonymous, free and open source.

show_hn.title: Show HN: Read the Room, a FOSS human bioindicator

quotes.text:
Hey HN!

Read the Room is an anonymous social polling app that lets anyone filter or compare results between generations, countries and cities.

Example: Rate "Is remote work overrated?" on a 1-5 scale and see if Gen Z in Austin agrees with Millennials in Berlin.

Privacy-first architecture: Response history stored locally on your device, only aggregates hit the server. Aiming for close to "zero-knowledge polling", Passkey auth (no passwords, no accounts). Each response to a poll is submitted as "City X votes +1 in bucket Y" without attaching the user to the response, or the fact that they responded to the question in the first place (all that is processed on device). Built with Flutter + Supabase, AGPLv3.

I built this slowly over a couple of years because I was tired of mass social media masquerading as surveillance tech, and I wanted to build what a "human bioindicator" might actually look like in an OSS paradigm. It's designed as a nonprofit, mirroring Wikipedia.

We're live at 500 installs across 50 countries with ~100 weekly actives right now, with vast majority of folks in the US/Canada. Though, it'd be cool to diversify that a bit more. English-only for now, but designing the multi-language support and will implement it once there is more traction.

Would love your feedback, and happy to answer questions!

Read more: https://readtheroom.site

Code: https://github.com/readtheroom-knowtheworld/readtheroom-app
